problemStatement.formal: For a graph G, the Goemans-Williamson scaffold defines SDP(G), expected rounded cut value, and alpha_GW=878/1000, then states GWExpectedCut(G) \ge alpha_GW * SDP(G) and SDP(G) \ge MaxCut(G).
problemStatement.plain: Backfill the MaxCut metadata around the Lean Goemans-Williamson scaffold: cut assignments, the conservative alpha_GW ratio, SDP and rounding axioms, endpoint checks for the rounding probability, and the final 0.878 approximation guarantee.
whyMatters: MaxCut is a canonical example where randomized rounding and convex relaxation beat simple random cuts.
The Lean development makes a useful proof skeleton even though SDP existence and the rounding inequality are axiomatized.
The entry should advertise the formal scaffolding while avoiding overclaiming a full analytic SDP proof.

proven: `GWCut`, `GWCut.edgeInCut`, `GWCut.size`, `GWCut.ofAssignment`, and `gwMaxCutValue` set up the MaxCut approximation vocabulary around the conservative 878/1000 ratio.
The ratio arithmetic lemmas verify positivity, the comparison with 1/2, the 7/8 and 9/10 bounds, and the 439/500 fractional form of the conservative constant.
open: `sdpRelaxation`, `sdp_ge_maxcut`, `gwExpectedCut`, `gw_rounding_inequality`, and `ugc_hardness_ratio` are axioms in `GoemansWilliamsonMaxCut.lean`; no active sorries were found.
knownResults.goal: Record the verified approximation skeleton and ratio arithmetic while clearly marking the SDP and geometric rounding inputs as assumptions.
